sentences.en: The illustrious glory of the eighth lot is hidden from me: in your own manner, even though your Muse grates horribly, teach it, I pray, while I stand by with attentive ears.
The approaches to heaven are not easy, nor are its gates wide open; one must struggle along a narrow path and seek it by a straight track, where the path points out a small threshold.

But still, there must be no stepping back and no loss of courage. The way that leads to the seats and joys of those above is steep, but it has been worn by the feet of many men whom the eternal Father has adorned with the honour they deserved.

This way, of course, is the one God took. Seized by eternal love, and not forgetful of himself or of our salvation, he took on human form and countenance on earth and, pierced through, poured out his soul through most cruel wounds. This way, I say, God himself goes first, flying on ahead, so that confidence may spur the brave all the more and shame may chastise the sluggish. He is weighed down by an immense mass, even though the cross is a burden on his shoulders. The rest of the youth follow him wherever he swiftly marks his footsteps, and as they follow they cannot match his mighty strides.

Since the series of events is very long, and it is enough to recount the punishments and deaths briefly, I myself will go on to tell you only the highest peaks as I follow them. You, turn both your eyes wherever I turn my finger as I teach, and store these things away in a mindful mind.

This one lost both his ears, and this one his right thumb. This one's hands fell off, and his nostrils too, from an unjust wound. This one was shorn with a stone, and this one was thrown down from a high watchtower.
This one is suspended from a straight beam, turned about by hands, and entangled at the feet. He is stretched by the weight of a clinging mass, and he grows as his whole body is distended.

sentences.en: That one perished, consumed by hunger and wretched toil, his eyes stripped of the defence of their tender rampart. This one falls amid the cracking of rods. That one, meeting the two-edged axe, falls forward on the yellow sand.
This one had his tongue thrust out, his hamstring cut and his body maimed. The executioners did not mock him as he grieved; instead they grieved as he laughed at his pains with a lofty mind.

A wedge went through the middle of this one, and through this one a pole with a point fixed to its end, and an iron-shod stake. A sword was driven through the side of that one, and streams of warm blood flowed. Goads were applied to this one. This one lies with his limbs cut and torn on every side. That one, given as prey to wild birds and wolves, hung aloft from a twisted rope while still alive.

And, what may astonish you more, woman and man plant their footsteps at an equal pace. Imitating the course of men and supported by choirs of virgins, a rival virtue flies on. And do men hesitate to imitate these deeds, and these men?
Does piety not drive its goads into us? Does the illustrious ardor of the virtues, spread abroad, not entwine fire in our senses?

Does heaven not kindle our strength, and does glory not raise our minds with hope? Warned, ah, let us at last follow better things. Let toil and constancy conquer the journey; let the rewards, and the will for what is right struck into our souls, urge our minds on.
May He bring us to ancient virtue and manly spirits; may the father himself, leader of the choir, and the hero Xavier rouse us.
Too happy, twice, three and four times blessed are those whose lot it was to perish by a cruel blade before the face of a grim tyrant, and those whom this one care gnaws.

sentences.en: The royal offspring who came down from the serene sky gave these counsels by manifold example, by deeds and by frequent warning. They were for those to whom, by His judgments, He promised the heavenly citadels and whom He wished to hold the high heavens with Himself: to prefer poverty of mind to the treasures of Croesus; out of zeal for virtue, to avoid permitted beds and marriage torches as if they were the foul weapons of Cupid; and to be always ready to depend on the nod of another.
Yet this is the way of counsel, and the undefiled mind that keeps the commands of God the Father is not conscious of any fault.

By this counsel of the Heavenly Ones a rich poverty is produced for you. Through it the mind, stripped of its own goods and rough to the world, is clothed in ethereal splendor and heaped up with the hundredfold interest of the heavens, until it gains possession of Olympus. Do not let it be enough for you to have heard these things. Let it please you to linger constantly, to walk step by step, and to tread in the footprints of Christ.

Dare, guest, to despise riches, and fashion yourself too as worthy of God, and do not come scornful to needy circumstances. Enter beneath the gables of a narrow roof, and allow yourself to be laid on humble hay and bedding.

Let it be fixed in your mind not to bear children, so that with virgin offspring and the adornment of snowy modesty you may surpass the womb of fruitful childbirth; nor will you make yourself like the barren oat.

Lo, I would pray that either the lowest earth gape open for me first, or the almighty Father drive me with a thunderbolt down to the shades, the pale shades of Erebus and the deep night, before I violate you, Modesty, or break your laws. For I have called Mary to witness, and the happy souls whom the temples of heaven receive, that I once vowed my life to you, greatest Ruler of the heavenly ones, content with poor attire and without a marriage bed, free of foul crime. But if perchance I could succumb to such a fault as to wish to ally myself to someone in the marriage bond, then he who first joined himself to me has taken away my loves; let him have them with him and keep them forever.

sentences.en: Do not seek to join your soul in profane marriages, O sacred offspring, and do not trust in loose marriage beds. Virgin men will come who by their blood will bear our name to the stars, and the descendants of their lineage will see all things turned and ruled beneath their feet, wherever the returning sun looks upon either Ocean. Hence too the golden palace of the starry heaven now receives on its throne the innocent, who have set out from their earthly seat, and they increase the number of the Saints at the altars.

King Iarbas is said to have set up a hundred altars to God, and more than a hundred temples, immense throughout his broad realms; to have set up the eternal watches of the gods, soil rich with the blood of flocks, and thresholds blooming with various garlands; and to have consecrated the wakeful fire. Yet with all these he will be judged unequal in merit to the single vow of obedience, nor will it be granted him to match the praises of so great a bond.
And not only do the profane gifts of the gentile Iarbas, when bullocks were slain according to the law by ancient rite, yield to this vow: loosening the covering and the fillets
of his consecrated head, the priest of old is surpassed, by the divine mouth. But even he who pours libations at the altars of the Christians cannot run alongside it with equal steps.
For this virtue soars above all things in its merits, the virtue by which all the renowned saints gladly and more swiftly obey divine commands and carry out their orders.

Behold, as I have learned them, I teach you the three counsels of the great Father, and the purpose that now stands firm in my mind. See to it that these things are fixed in your inmost marrow. MUSE: Believe me, these things will remain fixed and immovable in my mind.
It is not in our power, O guide, nor in the power of whatever there is anywhere of the purified race scattered throughout the great world, to pay worthy thanks for so great a gift.
If any divine powers regard the pious, if there is any justice anywhere, and a mind conscious of right, may Christ bring just rewards and grant that we may follow these counsels.

sentences.en: Soon you will make every kind of sin succumb to death, if you have clung with your gaze fixed on one of these four and have grown used to pondering the last fates.

Hence let Death come to mind, the final boundary of life, which makes royal sceptres equal to iron mattocks. By it your limbs will be loosened with cold as you struggle, and your life will flee with a groan beneath the shades, to be tormented there.

Behold, God himself holds up two scales in even balance and places in them the differing fates of the two. Whom the struggle condemns, and to which side death sinks with its weight, the outcome itself proves, when death has taken you from life and has set loose the struggling soul and the knit-together limbs.

There is no need then for Minos to shake the urn anxiously, summon a council, and learn of lives and crimes; nor does Rhadamanthus have anything to do, nor anything to force into confession: the things that anyone among the living, rejoicing in his vain stealth,
has deferred the sins he committed until a late death. There is no need of these, I say, when each one's own deeds lie open.

Yet the eternal abodes are not assigned without a Judge. One more just than they, God from the great Godhead, will come forth as Judge, unlocking every hidden thing of the mind and laying bare all works, to render to each his due.
O grief, alas! How great a trembling seizes my limbs even now, as I turn over the lot of these in my remembering mind.
Will the final day, the inescapable time of eternal punishment, and the mercilessness of cruel death bring you no help? And will it not profit you to remember these things?

sentences.en: O man, let it be fixed in your mind to remember those pools of Cocytus and the Stygian marsh while breath still rules these limbs. Draw yourself into the midst of the assemblies and the throng of the silent. Go, climb the mound, from where you may survey them all face to face in a long line and learn the faces of those who come, whom, if you remember, you know as your one-time allies in crime while the times allowed it. Among them are those who brought death on themselves with an unspeakable hand and, loathing the light, flung away their lives. How they would wish now, in the upper air, to endure both poverty and harsh toils!

There are those who hated their brothers while life remained, or struck a parent, or wove fraud against a client; or those who brooded alone over the wealth they had acquired and did not set aside a share for their own, and these are the greatest crowd; and those slain for adultery, and those who followed impious arms and did not fear to betray the pledged right hands of their masters.

How dreadfully the avenging Tisiphone, girded with a whip, now leaps upon them and lashes them, and, brandishing grim snakes in her left hand, calls the savage bands of her sisters! From here groans are heard, and the sound of savage blows, then the grating of iron and the dragging of chains.

There they raise dreadful cries to the stars, like the bellowing of a wounded bull when he flees the altar and has shaken the ill-aimed axe from his neck. Everywhere there is grief and terror and many an image of death.

Within, a monstrous hydra, fiercer still, with fifty black gaping mouths, holds its seat. Then Tartarus itself yawns sheer downward and stretches beneath the shades twice as far as the upward view of the sky to ethereal Olympus.

sentences.en: Here the ancient race of Earth, the Titan youth, hurled down by the thunderbolt, writhe in the lowest depths. Here too you will see Tityos, foster-child of all-powerful Earth, whose body stretches over nine whole acres, and a monstrous vulture with hooked beak, pecking at his immortal liver and his entrails, fruitful for punishment, probes them for its feast and dwells deep within his breast, and no rest is given to the regrown flesh.

Why should I mention the Lapiths, Ixion and Pirithous, over whom a black crag hangs, always on the point of slipping and looking as if it were falling? Golden supports gleam on high festive couches, and banquets are laid out before their faces with royal luxury; the greatest of the Furies reclines nearby and forbids them to touch the tables with their hands, and she rises up, lifting a torch, and her voice thunders.

Here are forms terrible to see, death and toil, and many monsters of various wild beasts besides: Centaurs are stabled in the doorways, along with two-formed Scyllas, hundredfold Briareus, the beast of Lerna hissing dreadfully, and the Chimera armed with flames.
There are those who must pray, out of love for the farther bank, that they may be able to be the first to cross the river's course.

For when life has left them with their final light, not every evil departs from the wretched for that reason, nor do all bodily plagues leave them entirely; and many things long hardened must become deeply ingrained in wondrous ways.

Therefore they are disciplined with punishments and pay the penalties for their old evils: some are spread out, hung empty to the winds; for others the ingrained crime is washed away under a vast whirlpool or burned out with fire.
Until a long day, when the cycle of time is complete, has removed the hardened stain and left pure the ethereal sense and the fire of simple air.

Be mindful to pay the sad shades what you owe of funeral rites, and let nothing of your duty rightfully be left undone by you. But do not do it in the human manner of men who care only for external things, and who ponder nothing in their minds besides processions and haughty pride. They are men miserably bewitched by the ruinous error of sad Avernus, or of that world.

sentences.en: For does it do any good at all to raise the lifeless Pallas to the stars with praise? He sends a thousand men chosen from the whole column to escort the last honour and to share the father's tears, a small consolation for a huge grief, but one owed to the wretched father?
What good is it to have active men weave a soft bier of arbutus rods and oaken wicker, and shade the raised couches with a canopy of leaves?

like a flower plucked by a maiden's thumb, whether a soft violet or a drooping hyacinth, whose brightness has not yet faded and whose beauty has not yet departed, though mother earth does not nourish it or supply its strength?
If meanwhile the soul is wretchedly snatched away from here to the waves of swift Phlegethon, to atone for its ingrained stain through everlasting ages, never to enjoy rest?
What good is it to spread out twin garments, stiff with purple and gold, which royal Dido herself had once made with her own hands, and to veil the corpse in this mantle?
And, besides that, to add many prizes from the Laurentine battle? What good is it that the booty is led along at the same time in a long line?
That the hands of those he would send to the shades as funeral offerings, to sprinkle the flames with their slaughtered blood, are bound behind their backs?
That the leaders themselves even carry trunks clothed in enemy arms, and that the enemies' names are fixed to them?
What does it avail that Aethon, the warhorse, his trappings laid aside, goes weeping and wets his face with great drops?

That others carry his spear and helmet? By ancient custom, what does it mean that the mournful phalanx follows, and the Teucrians, and the Tyrrhenian leaders, and the Arcadians with their arms reversed?
What do all these things avail? What help has the soul received by relying on this triumph, unless perhaps it finds relief from elsewhere?

sentences.en: Perhaps the Teucrians will be allowed to pay these rites to a barbarian people laid to rest in the earth, and this may seem enough, as for people ignorant of the faith, from whom the light has been taken away. But as for Christians, who have been given greater grace, who would deny that they are bound to do far better things for the dead?

For them it would count as the least of things to lead solemn processions, to have the squadrons run three times around the kindled pyres in gleaming arms, to ride three times on horseback around the sad funeral fire, and to utter wails. Such things are worthless to Christians, whose care is for serious matters. By them the earth is sprinkled with tears, and their faces are wet with them too. They make vows to God and load the altars with gifts.
See the funeral torches here. The way shines far off with a line of flames and marks out the houses far and wide.
We bring in bowls foaming with warm milk and bowls of sacred blood, we lay the soul to rest in the tomb, and with a loud voice we call out the last farewell.

When the mound of the tomb has been built and the funeral rites discharged, they cannot be torn away from the grave until the damp night turns the sky, studded with burning stars. Indeed, the third day removes the cold shadow from the sky when, beside the deep ash and the mingled bones of their loved ones, they pour out prayers, mourning from the bottom of their hearts. To this they add relieving the wretched circumstances of the poor, calming the untamed impulses of the flesh with the sacred bridle of fasting, and taming the wanton senses.

Thus the piety of the ancients once devoted itself night and day, with united strength and in two thousand ways, to cleansing souls from stain, ready to decree from the heart whatever help there was to the sad shades: until, little by little, a worse and tarnished age (oh sorrow!) has followed in this our time, when impious posterity and an ungrateful crowd of descendants have abandoned their turns of discharging their vows for the sake of the dead. Alas, a thing to be deplored with just complaints!
From that time the hope of Belgium ebbed and, slipping, was borne backward; its strength was broken, and the mind of God was turned away.

Meanwhile the Shades, shut in, cry out from the blind cave of their prison, beating their breasts with their palms: "Alas, my offspring, greatest part of our race, what are you contriving? Or where has your care for us gone?

sentences.en: Will you not at last look to see where you have left a parent weary with age? Meanwhile sad fates have carried me off to where I am girt with flames, where twice a thousand battle-lines of pains wander around me; and unless your prayers withstand them, I linger, alas, in punishments, for the hostile blaze to devour me.
Come now, do not at last be loath to remember us, bearing pious prayers and sacrifices to the powers of the gods, so that the Judge may not demand further penalties by fire.

These duties you must undertake, lest dread Styx torment you, and lest you be compelled, grieving after your sowings and driven by wanderings, to approach the sad sunless homes, the troubled places, like the shapes that, rumour says, flit about once death has been met: in a hollow cloud, as I have seen, a thin shade without strength, in the likeness of a spectre (a monster wondrous to behold), which, gnashing out a mindless sound, utters empty words and feigns the clapping of hands and the steps of one walking.

Look, you may draw out all the time given on funeral rites: let night rush on, and, for prayers, let Aurora in her rosy chariot have already crossed the middle of the sky in her ethereal course; it is right for you to devote three days to this just labour.
This way does not lead to heaven; instead, the left-hand path exacts the punishments of the wicked and sends them to impious Tartarus.

Thunderbolts hurled from the sky and blind fires from the clouds do not terrify our minds as much as the name of Avernus and of the lake of Cocytus. O God most good, see how sweat has burst out over the whole body and drenched bones and limbs. The companions' blood froze cold with sudden fear, their spirits failed, and their voices stuck in their throats.

sentences.en: You have the power to ensure that nothing delays the mind from reaching the pleasant green places of the fortunate groves, the blessed seats, and the joyful places where the soul may rightfully be granted to abide forever, unless you refuse to will it.

But why would the ardor of a heart so kindled refuse to will it for a wretch who seeks the heavenly realms, when he gave it even to the unwilling, softening their stony hearts with a gentle sound? God, gracious God, have pity on us, gnawed by the deepest anxiety over the crime we have committed. O how often are the rewards of the heavenly kingdom, and indeed, by your mercy, the first honors, restored to such as these?
But if, then, there are such great rewards for those overcome by crime, since you pity the fallen, what worthy gifts will you give to the just man who has earned the first crown by praise?
Will the compassion of Christ's heart, so great and so patient, allow us to pray in vain for pardon and for heaven?

But you, divine mother, confidence of our race, allow us, who call on you in our vows, to carry this hope in you: that you will always and everywhere support your companions with prayers. And since you are the interpreter of the gods, you who perceive your son's divine will, not through tripods, not through the laurels of the Clarian god, but through the stars, I pray you, sing, and willingly unbind your voice and lips:

Come now: Religion has declared that my whole course will be prosperous, and all the Saints by their divine will have urged me to seek Elysium and to attempt the remote lands. So unfold to me in words a few things out of many, so that I may cross the welcoming seas more safely and be able to settle in the heavenly port. For the Fates forbid mortals to know the rest, and the author of heaven forbids it to be spoken.

Here the Mother spoke: "O you who are dearer to your parent than the light, do not doubt: it is a manifest truth that you travel over the deep under greater auspices. This is how the King of the Gods allots the fates and has willed their changes; this is the order that revolves.

sentences.en: But Elysium, which you now think is near, and the neighbouring harbours you are ignorantly preparing to enter, lie far off, cut off by a long and pathless way across long lands. First the oar must be bent in the Trinacrian wave, the expanse of the Ausonian sea must be crossed by ships, and the lakes of the underworld and the Aeaean isle of Circe must be passed, before you can settle safely in the harbour of heaven.
Do not refuse the winding ways, and do not shudder at the courses still to come: the fates will find a way, and Jesus, when called upon, will be at hand.

* Seek the land on your right, and the seas on the right, by a long circuit; shun the shore and the waves on the left. † Scylla besieges the left side, and implacable Charybdis the left; three times, from the lowest whirlpool of her abyss, she sucks vast waves down into the sheer depth, then hurls them up again in turn into the air and lashes the stars with the wave.

It is better to take your time rounding the turning-posts of Trinacrian Pachynus and to bend your long course around it than to have seen even once misshapen Scylla beneath her vast cave, and the rocks resounding with her sea-blue hounds.
Let no loss from delay here count for so much with you. I shall explain how you may both shun and bear each labour, and, duly honoured, I shall grant you favourable courses.

These are the things of which you may be warned by my voice. Only go on, and direct your step where the way leads you; for by this way your ships and the youth of your people are either already in harbour or entering its mouth under full sail."

"I am resolved to obey your warnings, great Mother of God; my will is certain, and it is right for me to carry out your commands, so that at last it may be granted me to join right hand with right hand, and to hear and return the auspicious voices of those above."

sentences.en: O fortunate ones, whose walls are rising there! But better still is the lot of those whose fortune is already accomplished. We are called from one fate to another; for them rest has been won. They have no expanse of sea to plough and no fields of Elysium, ever receding before them, to seek. Meanwhile, happy, twice and three times blessed, is the one who, as soon as he looks up at the heights of that city, quickens his pace and directs his steps toward its walls. As he walks, God has fenced him about with a dark covering and poured a thick mantle of cloud around him, so that no one can see him or touch him, contrive to delay him, or ask why he has come.

Bring me in, I pray, O God most good, enclosed in this cloud, so that nothing but the divine may remain stored in my mind; for my mind shudders to remember anything profane. Let the one image of God, my dear Father, come to mind, and may I ponder the cruel fate of Christ alone. May the man's great virtue and the great honour of his praise keep returning to my mind, and may his features stay fixed in my heart. Let him be my life, my salvation, the guide of my life, the true path of salvation. From now on let nothing mortal touch me, and let death be gain to one who gazes on the heavenly kingdoms.
Long since worn out for the world, why do I, useless, drag out the years? Ah, if only I might now stand safe on my Father's threshold!
Look, we have crossed a plain of immense distances, and now it is time to unyoke the horses' steaming necks. As we depart from here, may God bring us to auspicious shores.

sentences.en: Mind of Christ, you who restore souls and fallen hearts, make haste to repair the ruins of the fallen breast, filling me with your divine presence as I wander through the empty void. May I be adorned with Astraea and the rest of virtue's garment, since the lofty glories of the supreme Father are gathering together.

The foul fluid of the heart has overflowed, and all my bones, shaken by disease, are little by little drawn in upon themselves. What is more, a parching fever rages within and feeds on my entrails, scorched with thirst; pain of every kind seizes my limbs.
What is left? I shall pursue Apollo's healing arts. Is he to bring the help of his art? It will do no good to have tried him.
…the assemblies and the Elysian fields: here chaste wines lead, flowing from your bleeding veins once the blood has been drawn.
Sweeter to me than unmixed wine is the very water of your rosy stream, O Christ: whom have these cups not made eloquent?
Away with you, cups of Bacchus that defile the mind, so long as these wines of honey-sweet blood gladden me.
O pure liquid flowing from the wound in Christ's side, wash from hearts the dregs of deadly stain, for the door of the King on high is open to no blemish.

sentences.en: O Christ, may the cruel scourges and the fierce blows of the spear-point driven into your flesh, on whose whole body no lash is dealt in vain, strengthen me with mighty strength.

Your death is life to me, so that courage may be lively in war while the arms of Cocytus surround us on every side. Father, hurl your flames into our breasts; victorious one, consume us with the torch, with the sword, with the same wound; grant that the offspring may go as a companion to the dear parent.
With you as our leader, we shall go as an offered victim to the death we long for, provided that your death brings forth life-giving beginnings for me.

O kindly guardian of your flock, most gentle Jesus, supreme Shepherd of the sheep, you who care for so many sheepfolds, which your loving-kindness never passes by with a deaf ear: do not, gentle one, refuse to heed the voices of those who pray.

Let me be granted the power to lie hidden in your wounds, above all at the rosy threshold of the pierced heart; for on these shores I shall always dwell in safety, until the grievous wickedness is atoned for and washed away by a fountain of tears.

sentences.en: It is right to pay worthy thanks to the King of Heaven and to exult in God in our souls for so great a gift, the gift with which His goodness deems us worthy, bringing the welcome gifts of salvation when He destines His own offspring for the altar.

He looks down from on high on the lowly lot of His handmaid. He does not shrink at all from dwelling in humble cottages and in the hidden recesses of the womb, but becomes a new guest in these dwellings through a virgin birth, with the flower of modesty undefiled, resolving to make me a parent through a divine offspring. Hence the office of Mother that I discharge is no empty one.

From now on every race of men shall declare me three and four times blessed, giving me a name that is eternal for all ages. As long as rivers run into the seas, as long as shadows move over the slopes of the mountains, while the sky feeds the stars, my honor, my name and my praises shall remain forever.

You grant, O nurturing Father, who hold supreme power over the world, that I may be not the least glory of the great Isaacid lineage of heroes, so that no single page may confine my virtue. Surely too great is the grace of my changed lot, while it is enough for your handmaid if you adorn her with the honours of praise.

sentences.en: Is he not able to curb the hunger of the empty mind, so that its hunger is taken away and the love of possessing is held in check?
And will he not be able to send the rich away in want of all things, those who once had been mighty with wide dominion?
A thousand ewe-lambs of yours now roam the Sicilian mountains, and fresh milk fails you neither in summer nor in the cold; yet perhaps tomorrow's light will see you stripped of your goods.

After so many thousand circuits, as the months rolled round, mindful himself of his promise and of his ancestral mercy, by which he willed to undo the common guilt of the world, he is brought forth by a happy birth into the air of light, in the manner of an infant, sprung from the blood of the sons of Isaac.

Come here, O beautiful boy. Look, the Nymphs bring you lilies in full baskets. For you the fair Naiad plucks pale violets and the tops of poppies, and joins the narcissus to the flower of sweet-smelling dill. Then, weaving them together with cassia and other sweet herbs, she sets off the soft hyacinths with yellow marigold. I myself will gather quinces white with tender down, and chestnuts, since we ourselves have loved these. And I will pluck you, O laurels, and you, myrtle, their neighbour, since, placed together like this, you mingle sweet fragrances.

sentences.en: Just as God had spoken with his own mouth to our fathers, to great Abraham and to his offspring and his descendants long ago.
So the Prophets solemnly open their mouths, as if at fate's bidding; we are sent here to seek the oracles for our fallen fortunes.

It is settled in my mind to render to the great Parent his due rights. It is equally fitting to give the Son, as far as lies in our power, the praise and honour he deserves for the triumphs he won over death. And my will stands firm in my heart to celebrate in the same way the Deity who proceeds from both Deities.

sentences.en: Come, kindly Spirit, sent down from high heaven, and grant that you may enter these dwellings of ours as a new guest. For you, great in divine power, desire to live in humble cottages and the unkempt countryside, under the turf-heaped roof of a poor hut, in mangers pleasing to the Thunderer.

Let this be your task, Life-giving Deity of heaven: to breathe into souls, which the right hand of the blowing breeze created out of nothing, the arms of your people as they strive; to have gifts upon their shoulders and fix crests upon their heads; to use the shield of grace and bear the Father's emblem.

You are able to soothe the sad sorrows of the mind and, by consoling with words and deeds, to drive cares away. You are a mind powerful in piety, preserved through a long age, no stranger to evil, and ready to help the wretched.

No equal to you is the sceptre once borne by Ilione, the eldest of Priam's daughters, nor the pearl-set necklace for her neck, nor the double crown of gems and gold. You are the immense gift of the almighty Father of Olympus.

I would count as nothing the gifts snatched from the ruins of Troy, the ornaments of Argive Helen, the wondrous gift of her mother Leda, which she had carried away from Mycenae when she set out for Pergamum and a forbidden marriage.

sentences.en: Add to these a mantle stiff with figures and gold, and a veil woven round with saffron acanthus: all these things are nothing compared with the one gift of the Thunderer.

You are the fountain of living water that leaps up to the lofty mountains of the heaven-dwellers; you are a fiery force, the flaming ardour of a mind kindled by the love of God; and you are a fragrant unction that brings back to you balsams sweating from scented wood, balsams that surpass by countless degrees the berries of the ever-leafy acanthus. You, finally, are believed to be the eternal Godhead, whom the stars of heaven obey.
You continually adorn your offspring with the surpassing adornment of the sevenfold gift: the Royal Majesty has made the lofty glories of the great parent common to the offspring.
You are the finger of the Father's right hand; you are, duly, the Thunderer's promise, enriching throats with the heavenly word.

Come, grant that ethereal light be kindled in the inmost senses, so that a manifest taste may give proof, and the sad mouths of those who try it may be tormented by a bitter sensation. So may the mind that has turned away from God learn its own deceits, and then, once the wiles are discovered, obey without turning away.

sentences.en: As the wicked crow calls for rain at the top of her voice and paces alone by herself on the dry sand; and as you may see the various birds of the sea, and those that search the meadows of the Cayster in its sweet pools around Asia, vying with one another to pour abundant spray over their shoulders, now thrusting their heads against the waters, now running into the waves, and exulting in a vain eagerness to lift themselves up: just so is it to be desired that fiery flames be sent into the cold minds of men, flames to lick the stars and raise up globes, and melted hearts, into the air.
Come then, blow through our heart with this vehement whirlwind, and, belching forth fires, mingle in bedewing blasts.
Grant, Father, that the worn limbs of my weary body be strengthened with vigour, so that my strength may return for battle.

We are overwhelmed by enemies, and an iron shower assaults me. Standing tall in the middle of the walls, the towering horse pours out armed men. Others are at the double gates, more thousands than ever came from great Mycenae. Others have set themselves against us and blocked the narrow streets with weapons. The line of iron stands with gleaming points, blades drawn and ready for slaughter. Who could resist in such blind warfare?
No one could, except those whom the Father of gods and King of men has breathed upon with the winds of the Spirit and touched with fire.

Drive the hostile battle-lines far from here, drive their weapons far away. In our right hands we bear the fillets and the words of those who pray, and a hand holds out the branch of the peace-bearing olive.

sentences.en: Let treaties be made. We all beg you for a peace that rests on God and is strengthened by the breath of the Godhead. Through it, even if not every evil leaves the wretched and not all bodily plagues depart entirely, hearts wounded by sins may still be restored, their deadly stain remitted.
With you as our guide, it is lawful to know the Father. And may we be granted the power to see the serene face of the divine offspring who founded this world with laws.

Praise to you, born of God, who triumph over conquered death, leaving the tomb and the Stygian marsh by your own power. May great fame, with well-deserved trophies, sustain your name, and may the good grace of your deed remain in the world. Let there also be equal praise and glory to the immense Father. And to the one who flows from both into the ages, let there be his own Godhead, equal radiance, grace and splendour, and an equal summit of honour.

sentences.en: Rest in sweat: for to its own, their hearts forgetful of their labors, the nourishing breeze gives peaceful rest and pours it through their limbs. Those it has cherished in its bosom it soon raises to the lofty groves of the heaven-dwellers, where soft marjoram, breathing fragrance, embraces them with flowers and sweet shade.
And when the scorched field swelters with dying grasses, then, with the power of God now breathed forth more closely, the divine breeze. With Zephyrs it tempers the fires of the stars.
O light high in heaven, twice and thrice blessed on earth, may you settle as a guest in the healed dwellings of the soul, hiding yourself in the inmost depths of our mind.

It will be in vain that the guilty are granted the name of friend, unless they accustom themselves to submit their necks, free from vice, to the Thunderer's command and to carry out the orders of Christ.
Come then, now that your anger is calmed and you have grown milder, sprinkle with the rosy stream of precious blood the minds defiled by deadly sin, and wash them clean.
Since dry things do harm, let the will be set on watering hearts, and let the South wind bring rains from the longed-for Olympus.

sentences.en: Grant the worshipper the honors that his own virtue promises; grant that he may close his completed day with a happy fate, and that glad times may follow for his wearied mind, so that together we may sing 'Io!' three times, and the paean, forever.

Hail, you who walk as Queen of the Heavenly Ones, at once daughter and mother of God, enriched by so many triumphs won, supreme mother of supreme mercy, life and salvation, Hyblaean glory and the trust of our race: at the commands of the Heavenly Ones I shall bid you hail once more.

We have left the borders of our fatherland and our sweet fields, and we wander around all the seas, driven by the fates. Alas, as fugitives and the pitiable offspring of Eve, we seek homes in exile, lying beneath another sun.
O you who alone have pitied the unspeakable toils of men, no stranger to misfortune, taught to succour the wretched, you who, on land and sea, us, the remnants of Adam,

now exhausted by every misfortune and in want of everything, take into fellowship in your city and your home: in our misery we call upon you in our prayers. To you the offspring of Eve, in this tearful valley of toils, stands weeping, sighing and drawing its voice from the depths of its breast, beseeching your divine power with strong groaning.

Therefore, kindly Mother, than whom none is more excellent at calling upon God with her voice and prevailing upon the supreme Father, turn hither now your two eyes of ancestral mercy, and turn the eyes of a merciful mind and of a Mother upon this race of Christians, so that after this wretched exile of life, with the earth laid aside, it may be able to behold Jesus and to gather the blessed fruit of your womb.

O clement, O loving of heart, O you who surpass sweet honey in sweetness, glory and pattern of snow-white chastity, great Mother of the Heavenly Ones, do not be loath to remember us, so that your people, destined to come beneath the great vault of heaven and to enjoy the promises of Christ through the long ages, may exult, rendering eternal thanks for the gift.

sentences.en: He who fills the sea, the lands and the heaven with his Godhead, who sustains this threefold work, proud in its vast mass, by the mighty effort of his immense right hand, and whom the heavens cannot contain within their spaces: it pleased Him to inhabit humble cottages and the hiding-places of Mary's womb, adopted as his own, to keep unviolated the faith of the cloister of modesty, and to consecrate chaste nuptials.

And He who, while Aurora rises in the morning in her rosy four-horse chariot, illuminates the globe of the world with the lamp of Phoebus, and who, when evening is spent and night now rushes from the Ocean, enveloping both earth and sky in a great shadow, supplies the shining Moon and the radiant stars by which you may find your way back through the friendly silences of the quiet night: behold, nine months after the breathing Godhead had filled the womb of the divine mother with His Godhead, He is brought forth by a happy birth into the shores of light. Presently, emerging from the womb as an infant while the stars marvel, He comes forth, most beautiful, from the fragrant virgin rose.

O Mother too happy, twice and three times blessed, who are heaped with so great an honour of the gift of the Heavenly Ones that He whom the vastest region of Olympus did not contain should choose to be confined, so as to hide Himself in the sacred virgin.

Happy one, celebrated by the melody of the voice of the Winged One, who was sent to unseal the hidden springs; joyful in the birth of God, while Godhead overshadows with Godhead; pouring forth delights from your womb and nursing hope at your breast, by which the vows of the forefathers' desire are satisfied. For you, O Virgin, grant that hope should have what it had hoped for.

Praise to you, who are sprung from the blood of the virgin Goddess, together with the heavenly Father and the divine breath of the Godhead; and to the threefold and one God be praise and equal power. Let there be equal dominion, to which the ages would deny that limits could ever be set, since they are the rewards of an eternal kingdom?

sentences.en: Hail, starry glory of the sea, you who traverse the heavens, daughter of the highest Father and at the same time nurturing Mother of your own parent, splendor of the virginal flower and eternal pattern of snow-white modesty, than which none is more excellent, you who unlock the happy approaches of double-gated Olympus; you who are worthy to return to heaven the sweet song of the messenger from the sacred mouth of Gabriel. Strengthen this offspring with the allied covenant of peace, and at the same time grant that the ignoble name of Eve may gleam with the light of the rays of your race.
Turning this way and that the immense coils of chains, do not hesitate to set free the guilty who confess their offenses. Surround blind hearts with the mantle of your sun.

Wherever in the world a place holds you as you pity our misfortunes, on whatever soil you reign in your great beauty, you will always be celebrated with my honor, always with my prayers. O be present at last, and look more closely upon things. It is lawful for you to ward off mortals from the perils of Cocytus; let it not irk your mind to come to the aid of wretched affairs.

Asking many gifts for your own, you will enrich the needy. May the sweet face of the maternal Deity favor me, and may you, as a suppliant, obtain that compliant ears incline to your words; and, removing wrath from heavenly minds, do not allow the Deity to be unfriendly to me.
With you as his Mother, may he be mindful that he was born of a virgin and given to sick mortals as a support of life.

O excellent Virgin, the confidence of our race, adorned in mind with the distinguished honor of piety, gentle in your outstanding devotion and chaste of heart, us, freed from all the polluted dregs of crimes,

lines.en: AMEN.

sentences.en: Come now, divine Parent, direct our steps, I pray; grant that the fleet may run a straight course over the clear sea. Do not let it drift and wander with its Master lost, but with its Mother's help let it sweep the blue waters unafraid, until it may come to rest in the longed-for harbour.
There the joyful may behold the holy face of the Deity and sing an everlasting song with sweet melody: Praise to you who are sprung from virgin blood, etc.

You surpass the Titanian stars with your manifold light. Behold, the almighty Creator, who brought you forth out of nothing into the breezes of light, once sucked at the breasts in your sweet lap, like an infant licking sweet things.

What Eve took away from her race by breaking the commands of the highest Father, calling down on it the wrath of the Deity, you restore to sick mortals by a happy birth. Hence those who once filled places far and wide with weeping, grief and sad laments are now glad through the divine gift, and they never cease to cry 'Io!' three times and 'Paean!' three times.
And so, Virgin, you become the gate of life for your offspring, since through you they enter the heavens by the double-opening gates.

You, O thrice-greatest care, seek gentle approaches to the King for your children, and you seek favourable times for their death. Let it be right for you to be called these things, gate by title on the one hand and window by name on the other; let it be your right, by divine lot, to be so called.

Applaud, happy souls, for whom this auspicious gate of salvation stands open. Grant that for me too the lofty halls of the heaven-dwellers may be opened, for you can do all things by a nod, as the Mother of the eternal Father, who has supreme power.

Praise to you who are sprung from the virgin blood of your mother, together with the heavenly Father and the divine breath of the Deity. To the threefold and one God be praise and equal power. Let there be equal dominion, a dominion on which the ages would deny that limits could ever be set, since these are the rewards of the eternal kingdom.

sentences.en: Hail, you who hold the lofty sceptres of the heavenly crown and have ruled over the assemblies of the Winged Ones for so many years now. Hail, O thrice-holy root, from which the golden light, carried by rosy chariots, rises from above upon the world. Hail, gate of the heavens that opens for the worshippers of Christ. Rejoice, immortal glory of virginal modesty, outstanding model of beauty, surpassing the radiant stars and gleaming with much splendour beyond the rest. Thrice-beautiful one, farewell. With your palms stretched out to the Godhead, may it not displease you to entreat our salvation with prayers, and by your prayers grant that we may joyfully obtain the heavenly seat.

Virgin, powerful to soothe the grieving minds of men by consoling them and to turn away the cares of the wretched with your words: by those highest joys that seized your heart when it was granted to you by lot to see your offspring, living again with death conquered, return once more to the ethereal stars and come beneath the upper breezes of heaven, I beseech you, do not refuse to help the doubtful affairs of the soul of your children, whom anxiety about Erebus torments.

You see how the ethereal Winged One carries the two scales in a doubtful balance, and how the images of two souls placed upon them are carried at once on this side and on that, each with a different sign, so that it may be revealed by a just distinction which one wickedness condemns and presses down with great weight to Orcus, and which one better virtue raises to the ether.
Alas, upon whom would the greatest horror of Hell not rush, when they are uncertain where the fates may call them and where they will be granted to stand?

sentences.en: Each one, with his crime made manifest, will plead his own cause for himself and alone, while the circle of those above and of men looks on. But He Himself will be King in the midst of the Winged Ones and of those who fly in heaven, and, sitting on a flashing cloud amid the light of the stars, he will learn the lives and crimes of men. What hiding-places, what hidden things will he not lay open here, he who grants the power to penetrate the inaccessible recesses of the mind?
Ah, how often, unknowing, under a false image of the truth, have I burst the breathing-passages of the soul with a deadly wound?

Has not a hidden error within us, one that escapes our notice, often urged that an unspeakable war be demanded against the omens of heaven and against the decrees of God, in perversion of the divine will?

Perhaps the seeds of divine flame, given in vain, lay hidden and concealed in the veins and did not flourish, kindled, in the bosom deep in the heart. They did nothing worthy of heaven, and by deserving well they did not make others mindful of them.

Ah, how often, too, at the waters of the river Lethe, drinking a draught that brings no true freedom from care, drinking forgetfulness, shall I be accused of forgotten duty, which must by right be expiated!
And so the wrath of God, not yet having sated its ancient grief, will make us pay for our offenses with heavy punishment.
If they trembled, fearful with dread (they willed their own fates, for the Saints were present), if horror stood around those whom their own virtue raised to the heavens for their merits;

what wonder is it that one whom many crimes weigh down as guilty should tremble with fear? You will be struck, wretch, you will be shattered by the storm, you dregs of wickedness; a grim abomination, a grim punishment, will await you, and you will worship God with belated prayers, unless the holy Virgin wins by her entreaty the aid of mercy for the one who asks (the mother surely not terrified in spirit to no purpose, and moved by the great peril of the struggling soul). For rest is won for him, and the whole haven lies at the threshold, for whom the Star of the Sea calms the swelling sea with her prayers: the innocent man, his breast protected by the heavenly prayer of Mary, will never be robbed of a happy death.

sentences.en: Come then, most holy divine Parent of Christ, prophetess foreknowing the future, Glory of the heaven-dwellers, since you can do all things by a nod (if I ask for no realms undue to my fate), grant that I may settle on Olympus, where it may be lawful to be joined to Christ and cherished by His countenance, so that I cannot sate my mind and may burn as I gaze, hanging in the embrace of the Offspring and on the neck of the Parent, while I fulfill the great love of the true Father.
Add at the same time erring men and contrite hearts, who desire from the heart to retrace their steps, to escape to the upper air, and to tread in the footsteps of the saints.

Many a victim will fall by our right hand before the altars of God; likewise we will duly declare her own honor to the Mother, mingled with the clarions of the winged ones and with sounding lyres, striving to surpass with sweet melody the Nymphs, to whom even Thracian Orpheus with his lyre would be compelled to yield, when he sounds the seven distinct notes in accompaniment to the rhythms, or strikes them with his fingers or an ivory plectrum.
